pictures.scene: Calame, Mountain Lake — a cold blue lake lying in under high mountains at evening, banks of lit cloud piled right across the sky, the last sun striking red and gold along the snow of the far peaks, black firs standing up out of the shadowed slope below them, a shore of broken boulders and tawny grass in front of it, one small figure standing alone among the rocks, and the still water running in across the foot of the picture, jesus crossed to the other side of the sea of galilee, …
pictures.name: pd_calame_mountain_lake

pictures.scene: Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue — a synagogue packed for a feast day under low stone arches, a bearded man in a tall fur hat and a striped prayer shawl carrying the covered scroll of the Law through the press with his eyes lowered, a young man beside him in a white shawl banded with green and blue holding his hand against his forehead, an older man standing at the reading desk with the book open before him and another bowed right down over it, a child in a flowered coat looking straight out at us from the front, and the women leaning over the gallery rail above in furs and embroidered headcloths, now the jewish feast of the passover was near, …
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a money changer in a black fur hat and a dark brown gown bent over his counting table, a small gold weight pinched between his fingers above the pan of his balance, coins and little heaps of gold spread out on the worn cloth in front of him, his wife beside him in a scarlet gown and a white linen headdress with an illuminated book open under her hand and her eyes drawn off the page to the scales, a round convex mirror lying on the table edge with a window and the street caught in it, and a shelf of books and a flask and an apple ranged along the wall above them, two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread, …
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Blommers, The Fisherman's Children — a bare-legged boy sitting at a scrubbed deal table in a poor cottage, holding up a little wooden boat he has rigged with paper sails and steadying it on the boards with his other hand, a knife lying beside it, and his sister sitting across from him in a white apron and a grey cap with the brown net she is mending gathered over her knees, the needle still in her fingers and her face turned to watch him, the brick hearth standing dark behind them and red and grey flagstones running out under the table, here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish, …
pictures.name: pd_blommers_kinderen_van_de_visser

pictures.scene: Jan Brueghel, The Sermon on the Mount — a great wooded hillside with huge oaks and beeches spreading their green and yellow canopy right across the top of the picture, and underneath them a vast multitude gathered out of every rank and country, hundreds of small figures packed close together in red and blue and yellow and black, countrywomen in white caps, townsmen in ruffs and tall hats, soldiers, pilgrims, old men leaning on staves, a mother with a baby and a little dog at the front, a woman in a gold satin gown seated on the bare ground, and far in among them Jesus standing bare-headed in a pale robe with a ring of light about His head, one hand lifted as He speaks to them all, now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them, …
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_bergrede

pictures.scene: Millet, Woman Baking Bread — a countrywoman alone in a dark cottage bakehouse, seen from behind in a yellow headcloth, a white shirt with the sleeves pushed back, a blue-green bodice and a heavy tan skirt caught up over a scarlet underskirt, both hands gripping the long wooden peel as she slides a pale round loaf in through the low mouth of the oven, the fire inside showing as a thin line of red along the brick, the great smoke-blackened beams of the roof crossing the dark above her, a poker leaning against the oven front and a litter of straw and chips on the stone floor at her feet, gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted, …
pictures.name: pd_millet_brood

pictures.scene: Kramskoi, Christ in the Wilderness — Jesus sitting alone on a low rock in a stony desert at daybreak, barefoot, in a dark blue-grey mantle drawn over a deep red robe, His shoulders hunched forward and His hands locked hard together between His knees, His bearded face drawn and His eyes lowered and fixed on nothing, a pale rose and grey dawn sky with one long bank of cloud lying behind Him, and the broken grey stones of the waste spreading away in front of Him to the bottom of the picture, withdrew again to a mountain by himself, …
pictures.name: pd_kramskoi_christ_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Friedrich, Moonrise over the Sea — three people sitting close together on the smooth dark boulders of a shore at nightfall with their backs to us, two women in cloaks, one with a red skirt spread over the rock, a man beside them in a brown coat and a blue-green cap, all of them watching the water, the moon just risen as a small pale disc in a band of orange light along the horizon, the sky above it barred with long violet and grey cloud, a track of broken silver running across the sea toward them, and a sailing ship standing off to the left with her sails dark against the last of the light, when evening came, his disciples went down to the sea, …
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_moonrise_over_the_sea

pictures.scene: Bakhuizen, Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee — one small open boat flung up on the shoulder of a breaking wave under a black sky streaming with rain, the single pale sail torn loose and bellying sideways off the yard with the rigging whipping free, a white crest towering over the bow in a wall of foam, the crew in terror all down the length of the hull, one man climbing the mast to haul the sail in, an old white-bearded man throwing out his hand toward the stern, others crouched low along the thwarts with their arms over their heads, and Jesus sitting quietly among them in the middle of the boat, a gull or two blown past in the dark astern, a strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated, …
pictures.name: pd_bakhuizen_christ_in_the_storm_on_the_sea_of_galilee

pictures.scene: Israels, Children of the Sea — three small children wading barefoot through the thin shining water of the shore, the eldest girl bent forward under the weight of a baby riding on her back with its arms round her neck and its bare feet hanging at her side, her own skirt kilted up and her face turned down to watch her footing, a younger child beside her in a white cap and a dark pinafore holding the string of a little wooden boat that rides on the water at the left, the flat wet sand reflecting them all the way to the bottom of the picture, and a pale blue sky with soft white cloud over the low breaking surf behind, at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading, …
pictures.name: pd_israels_kinderen_der_zee

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel, The Census at Bethlehem — a village under snow seen from above at sunset, a red sun hanging low through the branches of a great bare tree in the middle of the picture, a frozen river crossed by a plank bridge with children sliding and skating on it, a brick church and steep-roofed houses on the far bank, and in the foreground a whole townful of country people pressed in a dense crowd about the open window of an inn where the clerks sit at a table with the register, men in brown and ochre coats waiting their turn with staves and bundles, women carrying baskets, a small child in red running out of the press, a man pushing a cartload of brushwood past them, another sawing timber, a woman sweeping, and hens picking about in the snow at the bottom, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_volkstelling

pictures.scene: Marstrand, Churchgoers Arriving by Boat at Leksand — a whole parish coming over the water on a bright summer morning under a blue sky piled with white cloud, long narrow black church boats rowed in line across the lake and packed gunwale to gunwale with people in white sleeves and white headcloths, more boats already beached along the sand, the crowd climbing out and wading ashore among the boulders, men in black hats and knee breeches and white stockings, women in red caps and blue skirts carrying babies in their arms, children waiting on the rocks, and the wooden church with its onion spire standing up out of the dark firs on the headland beyond, they got into the boats and went to capernaum to look for him, …
pictures.name: pd_marstrand_kerkgangers

pictures.scene: Millet, Man with a Hoe — a labourer stopped in the middle of a stony field and leaning the whole weight of his body on the handle of his hoe, both scarred hands folded over the end of it, his back bent, his coarse white shirt and blue trousers stained with earth, his heavy wooden clogs sunk in the broken ground, his face lifted and worn out and his mouth open as he gets his breath, the cleared red earth and flints running away under him to the bottom of the picture, thistles and stubble on the bank behind, and far off across the plain a man burning weeds and another with a horse still at work, do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, …
pictures.name: pd_millet_man_with_a_hoe

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Elderly Man in Prayer — an old man seen close against a dark brown ground, his grey hair standing out from his head and a long grey beard spread over his chest, wearing a plain heavy fawn robe, his eyes shut and his face bowed a little forward out of the shadow into the light, his two big weathered hands pressed flat together in front of him with the knuckles and old veins picked out, and an open book lying on the table below with the writing catching the light across its pages, what must we do to perform the works of god, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_elderly_man_in_prayer

pictures.scene: Tissot, The Gathering of the Manna — the camp of Israel in the early morning with the striped red and white tent cloths pitched up the slope behind, and the whole people out on the pale sand stooping and kneeling to gather the small white grains that lie scattered over it, men bent double with both hands in the sand, one on his knees sweeping it up, others filling shallow baskets and wooden bowls, a man carrying a loaded basket away on his shoulder, and in the middle of them a young woman standing straight and looking out at us with a white veil over her head and a great wicker basket balanced on top of it, held up with one bare raised arm, our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, …
pictures.name: pd_tissot_manna

pictures.scene: Champaigne, Moses Presenting the Tablets of the Law — the old lawgiver seen very close against a black ground, white-haired and long-bearded with two dark horns of light standing up out of his hair, wearing a deep blue mantle over a gold-embroidered breastplate and a pink ruffled cuff, holding up with both hands a tall grey stone tablet turned full toward us with the commandments lettered on it in an old script and numbered down its face, a long gilded rod laid aslant across the stone under his fingers, and his face lifted with his lips parted and his eyes wide as though he has only just been spoken to, it was not moses who gave you the bread from heaven, …
pictures.name: pd_de_champaigne_moses_presenting_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Cotan, Still Life with Quince, Cabbage and Melon — a bare stone ledge coming forward out of total blackness, a yellow quince with two green leaves still on its stalk hanging on a thread high at the left, a great pale-green cabbage hanging on a second thread below it with its outer leaves curling loose, and a melon lying on the ledge with one deep wedge cut out of it so that the orange flesh and the wet seeds show, the cut edge and the ribbed rind catching a cold raking light from the left and everything behind them absolutely dark, whoever comes to me will never hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst, …
pictures.name: pd_cotan_brood

pictures.scene: Antonello da Messina, Christ Blessing — Jesus seen close and head-on against a plain black ground, His long brown hair parted in the middle and falling in curls at either side, a short beard, His dark eyes looking straight out at whoever stands in front of the picture, wearing a deep red robe with a blue mantle over the far shoulder, one hand lifted in front of His chest with two fingers raised in blessing and the other hand resting flat on the edge of a wooden parapet across the foot of the panel, with a small painted slip of paper fixed to the parapet below it, you have seen me and still you do not believe, …
pictures.name: pd_antonello_blessing

pictures.scene: Velazquez, The Adoration of the Magi — a dark stable with a broken arch and one small lit opening onto a hill and a pale evening sky at the top left, Mary seated in the middle in a rose bodice and a heavy dark blue mantle with a white veil over her head, her eyes lowered, holding the swaddled Child on her knee in a white wrap, the Child looking straight out at us, a king kneeling in the foreground in a gold-yellow cloak and black sleeves holding up a small covered cup with both hands, a second king standing behind him in a red cloak and a white ruff with a tall silver vessel, Joseph and another watching from the right, and a thin briar growing out of the stones at the bottom of the picture, for i have come down from heaven, …
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_adoration_of_the_magi

pictures.scene: Carracci, The Holy Women at Christ's Tomb — two women standing out on the stony ground at first light under the dark spreading branches of a tree, the first in a deep blue mantle drawn over her head and falling to her bare feet over a flame-red robe, one hand flung up open-palmed and the other pressed to her breast as she stares away out of the picture, her mouth just open, the second bent far forward beside her in a heavy white-grey mantle over a green gown with a gold sleeve, her head wrapped in white linen and her face turned down and back over her shoulder, one hand reaching out low in front of her and one sandalled foot thrust forward, a yellow-clad companion crowding in at the edge behind them, and far off at the left a pale strip of dawn sky over the hills with two small riders on the road, i will raise him up at the last day, …
pictures.name: pd_carracci_holy_women_at_the_tomb

pictures.scene: Millais, Christ in the House of His Parents — a carpenter's shop of bare plank walls with a long pale workbench running across the middle of it, a ladder, a saw and a set square hanging on the boards behind, a red-haired boy in a long grey shift standing barefoot in the wood shavings and holding up one hand with a small bleeding wound in the palm, his mother kneeling in front of him in a deep blue gown and a white headcloth with her face lifted and pressed against his cheek, a bald man in a red shirt with his sleeves pushed back leaning in over the bench at the right to take the boy's hand and look at it, an old woman in an orange shawl and a white turban watching from the far side with a pair of pincers on the wood in front of her, and curled shavings scattered over the floor at the bottom, is this not jesus, the son of joseph, whose father and mother we know, …
pictures.name: pd_millais_carpenter

pictures.scene: Dou, Old Woman Reading a Lectionary — an old woman seen close in profile against a dark olive ground, her white hair bound in a pleated linen band with a soft fur cap over it, a heavy dark blue gown with a wide fur collar fastened at the throat by a gold clasp, both gnarled hands holding up a great open book on its edge in front of her, the thick pages catching the light with two columns of close black lettering and a small woodcut printed in the middle of them, her head bent right down over the page and her eyes lowered and following the words, it is written in the prophets, and they will all be taught by god, …
pictures.name: pd_dou_old_woman_reading_a_lectionary

pictures.scene: Durer, The Vision of the Seven Candlesticks — a black and white woodcut cut in close dense lines, a majestic figure seated in the clouds in heavy folded robes with a long curling beard and a great burst of straight rays standing out all round his head, a long double-edged sword laid aslant from his mouth across his shoulder, an open book resting on his knees with the writing shown on both pages, one arm stretched wide to the left with seven many-pointed stars lying in the open hand, tall branched candlesticks standing in the clouds on either side with their candles lit, and a man in a thick mantle fallen on his knees at his feet with his head bowed right down and his bare feet thrust out behind him, only he has seen the father, …
pictures.name: pd_durer_the_vision_of_the_seven_candlesticks

pictures.scene: Gerome, Arabs Crossing the Desert — a party of riders walking their horses out across open sand in full sun, a brown horse and a grey one abreast in front with red and green worked bridles and tassels, the first rider veiled to the eyes in a black headcloth bound with a gold cord over a red robe and carrying a long upright lance, beside him an old man with a white beard in a tall white turban, a deep yellow robe and a green cloak thrown back over his shoulder, a steel shield and a silver-hilted dagger slung at his saddle, another horse and another lance crowding in at the right, two dim figures walking in the dust far behind, pale stony sand running away to the bottom of the picture and a bare blue sky going hazy over a distant red cliff, your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died, …
pictures.name: pd_gerome_woestijn

pictures.scene: Melendez, Still Life with Figs and Bread — a plain wooden table in a dark room with a round loaf set on it, torn open so that the pale crumb and the thick crust show, a second broken loaf behind it, a white dish heaped high with ripe figs, some split green and some deep purple with the flesh beginning to burst at the stalk, a horn-handled knife lying on the board in front, a tall black glass bottle stopped with a cork standing behind the bread, and a banded wooden pail and an ice bucket with its wooden pestle rising into the dark above, i am the living bread that came down from heaven, …
pictures.name: pd_melendez_figs_and_bread

pictures.scene: Juanes, The Last Supper — a long table spread with a heavy white cloth under a stone arch that opens on a green hill and an evening sky, Jesus sitting at the middle of it in a grey-violet tunic and a red mantle, holding up a small round white bread between his finger and thumb above his head and laying his other hand flat on his breast, a gold-footed chalice standing on the cloth in front of him, loaves, a knife, a salt cellar and a dish set out along the table, a white-bearded apostle at the left turning to him with his hand on his own chest and his name lettered in the gold ring of light about his head, a young apostle in green at the right leaning in open-mouthed with both hands raised, other hands pointing in from the edge, bare feet showing under the cloth on the chequered marble floor, and a great gold basin and ewer standing in the foreground, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the son of man, you have no life in you, …
pictures.name: pd_juanes_last_supper

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Supper at Emmaus — a dark room with a table pulled right up to the front of the picture, the white cloth blazing with light and a worked dark carpet hanging down over the front of the board, Jesus sitting behind it beardless with long dark hair falling at both sides of his face, in a red tunic with a white mantle over one shoulder, his face lowered and lit from the left and his shadow thrown huge on the plaster wall, one hand flung out wide and open over the table and the other stretched toward the bread as he blesses it, a torn loaf, a roasted bird on a painted dish, a split pomegranate and a wicker basket of grapes, apples and a pear set out in front of him, an old white-bearded man at the right starting up with both hands open, and the standing innkeeper crowding in at the left edge, whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, …
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_supper_at_emmaus

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, The Red Vineyard — a vineyard at the vintage painted in thick loaded strokes, the vines turned scarlet and orange and burning right across the whole picture, the pickers bent double among them in blue smocks and green aprons cutting the bunches and filling baskets, a woman standing straight with a flat green basket balanced on her head, another kneeling over a tub in the near rows, a wet track running down through the middle of the vineyard and catching the light in grey and violet and red, a blue cart and a horse up on the yellow ground at the top right, a line of dark trees along the far edge, and a low yellow and white sky with the sun in it, so also the one who feeds on me will live because of me, …
pictures.name: pd_gogh_wijngaard

pictures.scene: De Witte, Interior of the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam during a Sermon — a tall whitewashed gothic church with round pillars and pointed arches going back one behind another, daylight coming in through the leaded windows and their painted roundels of blue and gold, a brass chandelier and a carved organ case hanging high at the right, the preacher standing small and black in the raised wooden pulpit with one hand put out as he speaks, the elders seated in their pews below him under their hats, and in the near corner of the aisle a family listening with a child in a yellow jacket and white apron, a man in a black cloak, a woman with a white collar, a brown and white dog sitting on the sunlit flagstones in front of them and a woman in a long black hood standing at the right with her back to us, jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in capernaum, …
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_the_oude_kerk_amsterdam_during_a_sermon

pictures.scene: Hirszenberg, Head of an Old Jew — an old man's head painted close and large against a plain worked brown ground, a flat black cap pulled down over his brow, grey side curls hanging at his temple, a long white beard spreading right down over his dark coat, the skin reddened and furrowed over the cheekbones with deep lines running from the nose to the mouth, his heavy lids half lowered and his eyes turned down and away under them, the brush marks left standing in the paint all over the face, this is a difficult teaching, who can accept it, …
pictures.name: pd_hirszenberg_head_of_a_jew

pictures.scene: Mantegna, The Ascension — Jesus standing upright on a little round cloud high in a blue sky scattered with white cloud, in a blue mantle over a red-gold robe, barefoot, two fingers lifted in blessing and a slender cross-staff with a white and red banner held in his other hand, a tall oval ring of red-winged cherub heads closing round him with a dark band of cloud behind them, and far below on the rocky ground the apostles standing in a close crowd with their faces all turned up and their hands raised, Mary in the middle of them in a white veil and a red robe with her palms open, one old man holding a red book, a bare tan cliff rising at the left and a scrubby hilltop behind them, then what will happen if you see the son of man ascend to where he was before, …
pictures.name: pd_mantegna_ascension

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Denial of Saint Peter — an old bald man seen close against a dark brown ground, his high domed forehead deeply furrowed and his heavy brows drawn together over a short grizzled beard and moustache, his mouth just open and his eyes turned sharply aside and down out of the picture, a heavy dark brown mantle wrapped over a pale gold robe that falls in broad folds in front of him, both hands lifted in front of his chest with the fingers and thumbs turned back toward himself as if to say not I, and behind his shoulder at the left a dim fire burning low in the dark with sparks flying up from it, however, there are some of you who do not believe, …
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_denial_of_saint_peter

pictures.scene: Petersen, Emigrants on the Quay — a crowded harbour under a grey sky with the tall masts and rigging of a sailing ship crossing it and the great dark hull of a steamer rising at the right, a gangway running up to a deck where small figures stand at the rail, corded trunks, bundles and wicker baskets heaped on the wet paving, a young girl in a black hat and a pink apron standing in the near corner with an orange held up in her hand, a mother in a dark headscarf sitting on a chest with a small child in a green coat and a red knitted cap on her lap holding another orange, an old woman in a white cap and a black shawl leaning in behind them, a young woman in black standing against the wooden steps with her hand at her chin and her eyes lowered, a man in a blue smock bending over the baggage, a cab and a porter with a trunk at the left, and people waiting in every corner of the picture, from that time on many of his disciples turned back and no longer walked with him, …
pictures.name: pd_petersen_landverhuizers

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Saint Peter Preaching — a fresco in clear flat colour with a green wooded mountain rising right across the upper half and a pale stone wall closing it at the right, Peter standing at the left in a deep orange mantle over a blue-grey tunic, barefoot on the stone ledge, a gold halo behind his white head, his bearded face turned in profile toward the people and one hand lifted with the fingers raised as he speaks, a dense crowd pressed in at the right to listen, a young woman in a dark blue veil kneeling in front with her face lifted, a bald old man in a rose-red mantle kneeling beside her with his white beard and his head bowed right down, rows of heads behind them in blue caps and red turbans with every face turned toward Peter, and two men in long white habits standing at the edge, lord, to whom would we go, you have the words of eternal life, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_saint_peter_preaching

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Judas Returning the Thirty Pieces of Silver — a dim temple chamber with a great hanging ornament of gold plate and gold chains catching the light at the right against a deep green curtain, a high priest in a purple-brown robe with a gold sash and a white and gold turban turning away with his hand put out behind him and his face lowered, a man in a tall dark red cap staring out open-mouthed over his shoulder, an old white-bearded man pressing in at the left edge, a half-seen figure in a fur cap stooping between them, and Judas thrown down on his knees at the right with his bald head bowed and his hair torn, his hands wrung together in front of his face and his coat fallen open at the shoulder, the thirty silver pieces lying scattered over the pale stone floor at the bottom left where he has flung them down, he was speaking about judas, the son of simon iscariot, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_judas_returning_the_thirty_pieces_of_silver

lines.text: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, that is, the Sea of Tiberias.
A large crowd followed Him because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick.
Then Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down with His disciples. Now the Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.
When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip, Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?
But He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do.
Philip answered, Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.
One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, said to Him,
Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?
Have the people sit down, Jesus said. Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.
Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted.
And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples, Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.
So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.
When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.
Then Jesus, realizing that they were about to come and make Him king by force, withdrew again to a mountain by Himself.
When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea,
got into a boat, and started across the sea to Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet gone out to them.
A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated.
When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the sea, and they were terrified.
But Jesus spoke up: It is I; do not be afraid.
Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading.
The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not boarded it with His disciples, but they had gone away alone.
However, some boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.
When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, Rabbi, when did You get here?
Jesus replied, Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.
Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.
Then they inquired, What must we do to perform the works of God?
Jesus replied, The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.
So they asked Him, What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?
Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
Jesus said to them, Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.
Sir, they said, give us this bread at all times.
Jesus answered, I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.
But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.
Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.
For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.
And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.
For it is My Father's will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
At this, the Jews began to grumble about Jesus because He had said, I am the bread that came down from heaven.
They were asking, Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, I have come down from heaven?
Stop grumbling among yourselves, Jesus replied.
No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.
It is written in the Prophets: And they will all be taught by God. Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me,
not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father.
Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.
This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.
At this, the Jews began to argue among themselves, How can this man give us His flesh to eat?
So Jesus said to them, Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.
Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.
Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven. Unlike your fathers, who ate the manna and died, the one who eats this bread will live forever.
Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
On hearing it, many of His disciples said, This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?
Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching, Jesus asked them, Does this offend you?
Then what will happen if you see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?
The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.
However, there are some of you who do not believe. For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.
Then Jesus said, This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him.
From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.
So Jesus asked the Twelve, Do you want to leave too?
Simon Peter replied, Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God.
Jesus answered them, Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!
He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.
